text: So here's the verdict: there's no condemnation now for anyone who belongs to Christ Jesus.
The law of the Spirit of life in Christ Jesus has set you free from the law of sin and death.
The law couldn't do this, weakened as it was by our flesh, so God did it himself — sending his own Son in flesh like ours to deal with sin once and for all.
He did it so the law's righteous demand would be fully met in us, who now live by the Spirit instead of the flesh.
Those who live by the flesh keep their minds on what the flesh wants; those who live by the Spirit keep their minds on what the Spirit wants.
A mind fixed on the flesh leads to death, but a mind fixed on the Spirit leads to life and peace.
A flesh-fixed mind is at war with God — it won't submit to God's law, and in fact it can't.
People who are still in the flesh simply cannot please God.
But you're not in the flesh anymore — you're in the Spirit, as long as God's Spirit lives in you. Anyone without the Spirit of Christ doesn't belong to him.
If Christ lives in you, then even though your body is going to die because of sin, your spirit is alive because you've been made right with God.
And the same Spirit who raised Jesus from the dead will one day give life to your mortal bodies too, since that Spirit lives in you.
So we owe nothing to the flesh, brothers — we're not obligated to live according to it.
If you live by the flesh, you're heading toward death; but if the Spirit puts your sinful habits to death, you'll live.
Everyone led by God's Spirit is a child of God.
You didn't receive a spirit that makes you a slave again, cowering in fear — you received the Spirit of adoption, by whom we cry out, 'Abba, Father.'
That very Spirit joins with our own spirit to confirm that we are God's children.
And if we're his children, we're also his heirs — heirs together with Christ — as long as we're willing to share in his suffering so we can also share in his glory.
I'm convinced that whatever we suffer now is nothing next to the glory that's going to be revealed in us.
Creation itself is on tiptoe, eagerly waiting for God's children to be revealed in their full glory.
Creation was made subject to frustration — not by its own choice, but because of the one who subjected it — yet even so, there's hope,
because creation itself will one day be freed from its bondage to decay and brought into the same glorious freedom God's children will enjoy.
We know the whole creation has been groaning together, like a woman in labor, right up to now.
And it's not only creation — we ourselves, who already have the Spirit as a kind of down payment, groan inwardly too, waiting for our adoption to be finalized, for our bodies to be set free.
We were saved in this hope — but hope you can already see isn't really hope at all; who hopes for what they already have?
But since we're hoping for what we don't yet see, we wait for it patiently.
In the same way, the Spirit helps us in our weakness. We don't even know how to pray as we should, but the Spirit himself pleads on our behalf with groans that go beyond any words.
And the one who sees into every heart understands exactly what the Spirit means, because the Spirit's pleading always lines up with what God wants.
Here's what we know: God works everything together for the good of those who love him, those he's called according to his own purpose.
Because the people he knew in advance, he also determined ahead of time would become like his Son — so that his Son would be the firstborn among a whole family of brothers and sisters.
And those he determined in advance, he also called; those he called, he also made right with himself; and those he made right, he also brought to glory.
So what should we say about all this? If God is on our side, who could possibly stand against us?
He didn't hold back his own Son — he gave him up for all of us. So won't he freely give us everything else along with him?
Who's going to bring a charge against the people God has chosen? God himself is the one who declares us righteous.
So who's left to condemn us? Christ Jesus is the one who died, who was raised back to life, who's seated right beside God — and who is right now pleading our case.
So what could ever separate us from Christ's love? Trouble? Hardship? Persecution? Hunger? Poverty? Danger? A sword at our throat?
As the Scriptures put it, 'For your sake we're being killed all day long — they treat us like sheep headed for slaughter.'
But no — through it all, in the middle of it all, we come out the other side as more than winners, because of the one who loves us.
I'm fully convinced: neither death nor life, neither angels nor any other spiritual powers, nothing present and nothing still to come,
nothing far above us and nothing far below us — nothing anywhere in the whole of creation will ever be able to come between us and the love God has for us in Christ Jesus our Lord.
